findings.summary: Private generic cast helper centralizes type branding without enforcing a policy.
findings.consequence: The helper hides the actual trust-boundary cast behind a generic name, so future issuer additions can appear policy-backed even though the validation still lives entirely at each caller site.
findings.evidence: Line 10 defines a private generic `capability<T extends RenderableCapability>(value: string): T`, and line 11 returns the input via a direct type assertion. The direct callers inspected use named issuer functions after their own sanitization or managed-source checks, so this is not currently a confirmed behavior defect.
findings.recommendation: Either inline the explicit branded casts in each issuer, or rename/scope the helper to make it clear that it only brands already-validated or managed content and never validates input.
